newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed,gasoline firm on tight supp.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed,gasoline firm on tight supp.

text.p: Med oil products were mixed on Thursday, traders said. Gas oil climbed $1.50 a tonne with the IPE futures but supply remains healthy on growing refinery supplies after recent exports to Asia.
Russian cargoes held at perhaps 50 cents above the cif high quotes with 0.05 percent sulphur at just $1 above the quotes.

Dealers said they saw little local demand and some expected a slow trade over the next few weeks as demand shifts from Asia to the United States where prices have gained 3.50 cents a gallon over the past week.

Bunker demand diminished, with some potential fuel oil buyers changing their requirements. But overall, traders said markets had been quiet, with only Russian straight-run material being actively talked.

Although traders are still moving high sulphur material to the Far East many doubted that the arbitrage could be made to work further forward. They pegged Med fuel prices as steady to potentially weaker.
"I think some of the arbs must of shut, because of quality and loading problems with the available material," said one trader.
Gasoline was flat. Traders said the local market remained tight with demand out of Italy and the Eastern Mediterranean sucking up supply.
An Italian refiner bought an unleaded Eurograde gasoline cargo out of Lavera on Wednesday at quotes cif Med $-3.50 delivered into Genoa.
"The market's pretty tight," said one trader. "It would be higher but negative action on NYMEX capped it a bit yesterday."
The naphtha market was very quiet with sickly crude prices and lacklustre demand pressuring prices.
